sections.note: This class meets 3 hours per week in person; the equivalent of one additional class hour per week will be done online.

The Literature of Sports in Ancient Greece. This class introduces ancient Greek sporting culture through the available textual evidence, including epigraphy, epinician poetry, and narrative prose. Intersecting social issues such as physical and mental health, personal identity, and civic identity will be discussed. Previous interest in sports is not required.

Topic: In this seminar, we will use ancient accounts of Socrates’ trial to structure a close and careful investigation into the historical figure of Socrates and his cultural and intellectual milieu. In addition to close readings of relevant texts by Plato and Xenophon, we will spend considerable time looking at the portrayal of Socrates in Old Comedy; evidence and questions concerning ancient Greek religion generally (and, e.g., the Delphic Oracle in particular); accounts of the relationship between Socrates and Alcibiades; etc.
